title: candidate feedback draft - Hannah Lee
content:
Quick draft notes after loop with Hannah Lee (on-site loop 2026-03-11). Overall impression: strong systems thinker, solid latency/throughput tradeoff intuition, wrote clean code in the paired exercise but needs deeper familiarity with GPU inference primitives and quantization. Recommendation at end.

Role: ML Engineer - Serving Runtime (inference infra)
Interviewers: Priya Desai (runtime), Jordan Sanchez (sre), Ethan Hu (systems)

1) Technical - algorithms & complexity (score 4/5)
- Hannah explained transformer attention complexity well and reasoned through cache sharding tradeoffs for long-context workloads.
- Good at articulating time/space complexity and clear when to favor CPU pre-processing vs GPU batching.
- Minor gap: less confident on lower-level kernel tuning details (e.g., memory coalescing).

2) System design (score 4/5)
- Designed an inference service for multimodal requests: covered request routing, autoscaling, canary rollout plan, KV cache invalidation strategy.
- Thoughtful about SLOs and fallback to cheaper models under load.
- Would like to see more detailed metrics plan (what to expose for debugging per-request latency percentiles).

3) Inference/runtime knowledge (score 3/5)
- Familiar with standard optimizations (batching, caching, quantization) at a conceptual level.
- Less hands-on experience with quantized kernels, Triton optimization knobs, and some device-level profiling tools (nsight, nvprof).
- Has used ONNX/TF-TRT in previous role but not heavily for large-scale LLM serving.

4) Coding exercise (score 4/5)
- Pair-programmed a simplified request router and batcher. Code clear, test-first approach, added small unit tests.
- Edge cases handled (timeouts, partial batch flush). Performance micro-optimizations left as TODOs but structure supports them.

5) Culture & communication (score 5/5)
- Clear communicator, concise explanations, responsive to feedback in the loop.
- Collaborative, asked great clarifying questions and proposed pragmatic rollout plans that balance risk and velocity.

Strengths:
- Systems-level reasoning and clear ownership mindset.
- Strong product sense (understands developer UX tradeoffs when designing APIs and SLOs).
- Quick learner; explained how she'd ramp on kernel-level profiling and mentioned prior experience picking up new toolchains fast.

Concerns / Risks:
- Not yet deep hands-on experience with GPU kernel tuning and quantization flows we rely on for tight latency targets. This is rampable but would need mentorship from a senior engineer in first 3-6 months.
- Limited exposure to Triton / custom CUDA kernels (could be important for certain Dedicated/private workloads).

Interview-specific notes:
- Priya: liked the design choices but called out need for more explicit observability metrics in the plan.
- Jordan: happy with the SLO-focused approach and operational thinking; flagged quantization gap.

Suggested follow-ups:
- Quick take-home task: profile a simple model with and without int8 quantization and write 1-page notes on observed latency/quality tradeoffs (helps evaluate practical quantization comfort).
- Optional technical screen focusing on CUDA/triton profiling if we want to be conservative on kernel expertise.

Hiring recommendation: Strong hire with technical ramp plan. Candidate scores well on systems and culture; recommend hire at IC3-IC4 (depending on how aggressive we want kernel expertise earlier). Suggest offer band: $170k-$190k base (US competitive range) + equity and standard benefits.

Drafting notes: leaving as draft — will sync with hiring committee (Priya/Jordan) before moving to final. Need to attach take-home assignment if committee requests.

Action items:
- Share draft with Priya and Jordan for comments (ETA 2026-03-13).
- If greenlit, prepare offer packet and schedule follow-up take-home (owner: Ethan Hu).

Notes to self: keep the take-home focused and time-boxed (3-4 hours), include data to reproduce profiling locally (small model + helper scripts).
